newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - Alcatel unveils ambitious plans for Thomson.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Alcatel unveils ambitious plans for Thomson.

text.p: France's Alcatel Alsthom SA on Wednesday unveiled plans to build state-owned Thomson SA into the world's number two defence electronics company and a big consumer electronics group.
Chairman Serge Tchuruk told a news conference he would look for a European defence partner and an Asian partner for consumer electronics but the group had not decided on identities yet.
He shied away from giving financial details and declined to comment on reports the state might have to pump between five and eight billion francs into loss-making Thomson before the deal.
"It is up to the government to decide whether a capital increase is needed," Tchuruk said.
Alcatel submitted its offer on Monday. The sole other bidder is Lagardere Groupe which has waged a very public campaign to obtain the favour of the government.
The government is expected to decide in the next five to six weeks and the deal will take place before the end of the year.

Tchuruk said Alcatel wanted to acquire Thomson SA as a whole, which means both the profitable 58-percent Thomson-CSF as well as the loss-making Thomson Multimedia consumer electronics group. Thomson SA has debts of 25 billion francs, of which 14 billion at Thomson Multimedia.
Lagardere has lined up Korea's Daewoo to run Thomson Multimedia and get the group back in the black.

Tchuruk said that Alcatel would seek a "wide scale partnership with another major industrial player of the (defence) sector" to hoist Thomson-CSF to the rank of the world's number two defence group, overtaking GM Hughes Electronics Corp but staying behind Lockheed Martin.

Tchuruk confided to reporters that it would be "logical" Alcatel studied such a partnership with Britain's GEC Plc, its joint-venture partner in the GEC-Alsthom industrial power and high speed train company. But he did not exclude others and said he prefered to keep his options open.
Lagardere has named British Aerospace Plc and Daimler-Benz's DASA as potential partners if it wins the beauty contest.
Tchuruk said that a combination of Alcatel's and Thomson-CSF's technologies would make a leader in defence communication networks which are becoming more and more important in modern warfare.
He said Alcatel planned to buy out the minority shareholders in Thomson-CSF and take the group off the bourse.

For Thomson Multimedia, already the number one television company in the U.S. with the RCA and General Electric brands and number two in Europe behind Dutch Philips Industries, Tchuruk also had big ambitions.
In the world consumer electronics market, Thomson Multimedia ranks fourth behind Sony Corp and Mitsubishi Corp of Japan and Philips.
Firstly he noted that the increasing digitalisation of products was creating new markets by linking consumer electronics with communications networks.

Secondly he said that the group would need to restructure its "old" business of television sets and video recorders -- reducing the number of its brands in Europe from six and cutting costs -- and forge ahead in the digital world, building on its leading position in decoders.

Tchuruk said he would look for an Asian partner to bring both market access to the southeast Asian countries as well as expertise in efficient production. He declined to speculate on a name and also made no comment on rumours the Asian partner could take up to 35 percent in Thomson Multimedia.
Tchuruk said the Thomson deal would enhance shareholder value in the medium term and not deteriorate earnings per share in the short term. He added it would not hurt group debt ratios.
Alcatel's shares rose on a lower Paris Bourse as the market digested the proposal but analysts said the financing plans remained vague and the earnings per share promise seemed rosy.
